column5: The MD5 initialization routine stores this table at offset zero of the context. Its five words give the init, update, final, and one-shot hash entry points followed by the 16-byte digest size.
The update routine calls this compression function when its 64-byte buffer is full. The 64 MD5 rounds and four state accumulators identify the entry in each slice.
First function pointer of the MD5 dispatch table. Initializes the four standard MD5 state words and zeroes the byte count.
Second function pointer of the MD5 dispatch table. Streams bytes into the 64-byte buffer and calls the compression routine on full blocks.
Third function pointer of the MD5 dispatch table. Pads the input and emits the four little-endian digest words.
Each executable has one copy of all 64 little-endian MD5 additive constants. The compression loop indexes this table by round number.
The complete 64-byte MD5 rotation schedule occurs once in each executable's __TEXT,__const and immediately follows the 64 additive constants.

In gad_md5.o the finalization routine refers to two zero bytes at the beginning of __TEXT,__const. Four-byte alignment places the MD5 round constants at offset four in that same input section. Both executables preserve those adjacent input data and the two zeros.
